newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Tribesmen of murdered Brazil indian claim ranch.
newsitem.headline: Tribesmen of murdered Brazil indian claim ranch.

text.p: Angered fellow tribesmen of a native Brazilian Indian who was torched alive earlier this week on Wednesday invaded a ranch that bordered on their reserve claiming the land belonged to them, a government official said.

Rosangela Carvalho, the deputy head of Brazil's National Indian Foundation (Funai), said around 300 indians of the Pataxo tribe took advantage of the media attention surrounding the death of one of their tribesmen to recover the land.
"They seized the moment in which society was best predisposed towards them," Carvalho said in a telephone interview.

Galdino dos Santos, a leader of the Pataxo tribe from the northeastern state of Bahia, died of severe burns in a Brasilia hospital on Monday after he was soaked in a flammable liquid and set on fire by five middle-class youths.
Police said the youths torched Santos, who was lying asleep at a bus stop, as part of a "teen-age prank" after returning home from a night on the town.
All five youths have been arrested and charged and could face up to 30 years in prison if found guilty of murder.
Santos was in Brasilia together a group of fellow tribesmen in an attempt to speed-up a 15 year-old court case over the neighbouring property which they claim was taken from them by cattle ranchers.

Television pictures showed the Pataxo indians in full battle dress and carrying clubs, bows and arrows as they marched into the 750 hectare property that borders with their reserve in the municipality of Pau Brasil, in Bahia state.
The indians were also shown threatening ranch employees and knocking-down the doors and windows of a house on the property.
"We Indians must take that which belongs to us," Pataxo chief Wilson Pataxo told reporters on the scene.
Carvalho said the Funai had asked the Federal Police to protect the indians on the property for fear that they might be attacked by the owners of the ranch.

The brutal murder of Santos triggered a massive public outcry and focused media attention on the fate of the Brazil's native Indian communities who are routinely subjected to abuse by landowners and mining communties.
